Neonatal Incubator Display Reader Model training and evaluation¶

This notebook demonstrates the complete end-to-end workflow for developing an automated system to detect and extract vital sign readings from neonatal incubator displays.

Train detector model to locate vital sign regions¶

1: Run Overview¶

  • Creates run directory under artifacts/runs/<timestamp>
  • Uses YOLO-formatted data under artifacts/yolo (images + labels)
  • Steps: data check → split + data.yaml → train with early stopping → eval + plots → qualitative preds → export weights → save config/metrics
In [18]:

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

SAMPLES_PNG = RUN_ROOT / "samples.png"

def plot_samples(paths, n=6, cols=3):
    if not paths:
        print("No raw images to plot.")
        return
    sample = random.sample(paths, min(n, len(paths)))
    rows = int(np.ceil(len(sample)/cols))
    plt.figure(figsize=(4*cols, 3*rows))
    for i,p in enumerate(sample,1):
        img = cv2.cvtColor(cv2.imread(str(p)), cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
        plt.subplot(rows, cols, i)
        plt.imshow(img); plt.title(p.name); plt.axis("off")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(SAMPLES_PNG, dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.show()
    print(f"Saved samples -> {SAMPLES_PNG}")

4: Annotation Workflow with Label Studio¶

Objective: Create bounding box annotations for each vital sign region in the incubator display.

Tool: Label Studio - an open-source data labeling platform

Setup Instructions:

  1. Install Label Studio (one-time setup):

    pip install label-studio
label-studio start --port 8080

  2. Create a new project named "Incubator Display Detection"

  3. Import images from the dataset/ directory

  4. Configure the labeling interface with bounding box tool for the following classes:

    • air_temp_value
    • heart_rate_value
    • humidity_value
    • skin_temp_value
    • spo2_value

  5. Annotate all images

  6. Export annotations in YOLO format

5: Split YOLO Data & Write data.yaml¶

Uses existing YOLO-format data in artifacts/yolo/images and artifacts/yolo/labels. Creates train/val/test splits under the run directory and writes data.yaml there.

In [41]:
import yaml
from pathlib import Path

def normalize_labels(images_dir: Path, labels_dir: Path, out_dir: Path) -> int:
    """
    Copy labels into out_dir renamed to match image basenames, allowing prefixed label stems.
    Returns count of matched pairs.
    """
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    labels = list(labels_dir.glob("*.txt"))

    def find_label_for_image(img_stem: str):
        for lbl in labels:
            if lbl.stem.endswith(img_stem):
                return lbl
        return None

    copied, missing = 0, []
    for img in images_dir.glob("*"):
        if img.suffix.lower() not in {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".bmp"}:
            continue
        match = find_label_for_image(img.stem)
        if match:
            shutil.copy2(match, out_dir / f"{img.stem}.txt")
            copied += 1
        else:
            missing.append(img.name)
    if missing:
        print(f"Missing labels for {len(missing)} images (showing up to 10): {missing[:10]}")
    print(f"Normalized labels copied: {copied} -> {out_dir}")
    return copied

def split_dataset(yolo_dir, train=0.7, val=0.2, test=0.1, seed=SEED):
    assert math.isclose(train+val+test, 1.0, rel_tol=1e-6)
    yolo_dir = Path(yolo_dir)
    images_dir = yolo_dir / "images"
    raw_labels_dir = yolo_dir / "labels"
    norm_labels_dir = yolo_dir / "labels_normalized"

    if not images_dir.exists() or not raw_labels_dir.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"YOLO images/labels missing under {yolo_dir}")

    # Normalize labels to match image basenames
    normalize_labels(images_dir, raw_labels_dir, norm_labels_dir)

    imgs = []
    for ext in (".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".bmp", ".JPG", ".JPEG", ".PNG"):
        imgs.extend(images_dir.glob(f"*{ext}"))
    if not imgs:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"No images in {images_dir}")

    pairs, missing = [], []
    for img in sorted(imgs):
        label = norm_labels_dir / f"{img.stem}.txt"
        if not label.exists():
            missing.append(img.name)
            continue
        pairs.append((img, label))
    if missing:
        print(f"Skipping {len(missing)} images without labels after normalization")
    if not pairs:
        raise FileNotFoundError("No image/label pairs found")

    rng = random.Random(seed); rng.shuffle(pairs)
    n = len(pairs); tc = int(n * train); vc = tc + int(n * val)
    splits = {"train": pairs[:tc], "val": pairs[tc:vc], "test": pairs[vc:]}

    split_root = Path(SPLITS_DIR)
    for split, items in splits.items():
        img_out, lbl_out = split_root / split / "images", split_root / split / "labels"
        img_out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); lbl_out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for img, lbl in items:
            shutil.copy2(img, img_out / img.name)
            shutil.copy2(lbl, lbl_out / lbl.name)
    print({k: len(v) for k, v in splits.items()})
    return split_root

def write_data_yaml(split_root, class_names, filename="data.yaml"):
    data = {
        "path": str(split_root),
        "train": "train/images",
        "val": "val/images",
        "test": "test/images",
        "nc": len(class_names),
        "names": class_names
    }
    path = split_root / filename
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        yaml.dump(data, f, default_flow_style=False)
    return path

split_root = split_dataset(YOLO_DATA_DIR)
data_yaml_path = write_data_yaml(split_root, CLASS_NAMES)
print(f"data.yaml -> {data_yaml_path}")

6: Train YOLOv8 detector model with Early Stopping¶

  • Max epochs: 100
  • Early stop patience: 10 (stop when val stops improving)
  • Seeds set for reproducibility Artifacts stay under this run folder; prior runs remain intact.
In [43]:
import torch
from torch.serialization import add_safe_globals
from ultralytics.nn.tasks import DetectionModel
from ultralytics.nn import modules as yolo_modules
from torch.nn import modules as torch_nn_modules

# Allowlist Ultralytics/Torch classes for torch.load
add_safe_globals(
    [DetectionModel]
    + [obj for obj in vars(yolo_modules).values() if isinstance(obj, type)]
    + [obj for obj in vars(torch_nn_modules).values() if isinstance(obj, type)]
)

# Backward-compatible torch.load
if not hasattr(torch, "_orig_load"):
    torch._orig_load = torch.load

def _compat_load(*args, **kwargs):
    kwargs.setdefault("weights_only", False)
    return torch._orig_load(*args, **kwargs)

torch.load = _compat_load


def train_detector(data_yaml, epochs=100, imgsz=640, batch=16, model="yolov8n.pt",
                   project=RUN_ROOT/"train", name="exp", patience=10):
    model = YOLO(model)
    results = model.train(
        data=str(data_yaml),
        epochs=epochs,
        imgsz=imgsz,
        batch=batch,
        patience=patience,
        seed=SEED,
        project=str(project),
        name=name,
        exist_ok=True,
    )
    return model, results

print(f"Run directory: {RUN_ROOT}")
detector, train_results = train_detector(data_yaml_path)

In [44]:






def evaluate_detector(model, data_yaml, dest_root: Path):
    metrics = model.val(data=str(data_yaml), save=True)
    summary = {k: float(v) for k,v in metrics.results_dict.items()}
    metrics_path = dest_root / "val_metrics.json"
    metrics_path.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    print(f"Saved metrics -> {metrics_path}")
    # Copy val plots
    plot_src = Path(metrics.save_dir)
    plot_dst = dest_root / "eval_plots"
    plot_dst.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for f in plot_src.glob("*.*"):
        try:
            shutil.copy2(f, plot_dst / f.name)
        except Exception:
            pass
    print(f"Copied plots -> {plot_dst}")
    return summary

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

PRED_DIR = RUN_ROOT / "preds"
PRED_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

def visualize_predictions(model, image_paths, class_names, conf=0.25, max_images=3, save_dir=PRED_DIR):
    if not image_paths:
        print("No raw images available for visualization.")
        return
    subset = random.sample(image_paths, min(len(image_paths), max_images))
    for path in subset:
        res = model.predict(source=str(path), conf=conf, verbose=False)
        img_bgr = res[0].plot()
        out_path = save_dir / f"pred_{path.stem}.png"
        cv2.imwrite(str(out_path), img_bgr)
        # Show inline (convert BGR -> RGB for correct colors)
        img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(img_bgr, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
        plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
        plt.imshow(img_rgb)
        plt.title(path.name)
        plt.axis("off")
        plt.show()
        print(f"Saved {out_path}")

9: Export Best Weights¶
Copies the best checkpoint into this run folder and also into models/ (without overwriting prior runs).


















In [46]:






BEST_TARGET = RUN_ROOT / "incubator_yolov8n.pt"

def export_best_weights(run_dir=None, target_path=BEST_TARGET, source_path=None):
    def collect(candidate):
        paths = []
        if candidate is None: return paths
        candidate = Path(candidate)
        if candidate.is_file(): paths.append(candidate)
        elif candidate.is_dir():
            default_best = candidate/"weights"/"best.pt"
            if default_best.exists(): paths.append(default_best)
            paths.extend(candidate.glob("**/best.pt"))
        return paths
    seen, ordered = set(), []
    for item in collect(source_path) + collect(run_dir):
        if item.exists() and item not in seen:
            seen.add(item); ordered.append(item)
    if not ordered:
        print("No best.pt found"); return None
    chosen = ordered[0]
    target_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if not target_path.exists() or target_path.resolve() != chosen.resolve():
        shutil.copy2(chosen, target_path)
        print(f"Exported {chosen} -> {target_path}")
    else:
        print(f"Weights already at {target_path}")
    # also place a copy in models/ with run tag
    models_copy = MODEL_DIR / f"incubator_{RUN_TAG}.pt"
    shutil.copy2(target_path, models_copy)
    print(f"Copied to {models_copy}")
    return target_path

export_best_weights(run_dir=RUN_ROOT / "train")

  • Run detector → crop ROIs → OCR values → annotated image.

In [65]:






import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def visualize_ocr_grid(image_paths, detector, max_rows=6, conf=0.25, save_path=None):
    if not image_paths:
        print("No images available."); return
    img_path = random.choice(image_paths)
    res = detector.predict(source=str(img_path), conf=conf, verbose=False)[0]
    if res.boxes is None or len(res.boxes) == 0:
        print(f"No detections in {img_path.name}"); return

    rows_data = []
    for box_data in res.boxes:
        cls_id = int(box_data.cls[0].cpu().item())
        name = ID_TO_CLASS_NAME.get(cls_id, f"class_{cls_id}")
        if name not in NUMERIC_CLASSES:
            continue
        bbox = box_data.xyxy[0].cpu().numpy().astype(int)
        img = cv2.imread(str(img_path))
        x1, y1, x2, y2 = bbox
        roi = img[y1:y2, x1:x2]
        processed = preprocess_roi(roi) if roi is not None and roi.size > 0 else None
        text, conf_ocr = extract_value(roi)
        rows_data.append((name, roi, processed, text, conf_ocr, y1))

    if not rows_data:
        print(f"No numeric detections in {img_path.name}"); return

    # Sort top-to-bottom
    rows_data = sorted(rows_data, key=lambda r: r[5])[:max_rows]

    n = len(rows_data)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(n, 3, figsize=(10, 3*n))
    if n == 1:
        axes = [axes]  # make iterable
    for i, (name, roi, processed, text, conf_ocr, _) in enumerate(rows_data):
        # Original
        axes[i][0].imshow(cv2.cvtColor(roi, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB))
        axes[i][0].set_title(f"{name}\nOriginal ROI")
        axes[i][0].axis("off")
        # Processed
        axes[i][1].imshow(processed, cmap="gray")
        axes[i][1].set_title("Preprocessed\n(Enhanced for OCR)")
        axes[i][1].axis("off")
        # OCR result
        axes[i][2].axis("off")
        axes[i][2].text(
            0.05, 0.5,
            f"Value: {text if text is not None else 'None'}\nConf: {conf_ocr:.3f}",
            fontsize=12, va="center"
        )

    plt.suptitle(f"OCR debug: {img_path.name}", fontsize=14)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

    if save_path:
        fig.savefig(save_path, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
        print(f"Saved grid -> {save_path}")

# Run on a random image and show inline; also save to the run folder
visualize_ocr_grid(image_paths, detector, max_rows=6, conf=0.25, save_path=RUN_ROOT / "ocr_debug.png")
